A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniSapiens-7B 2.0 and HARPO. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original HARPO training comparisons, held-out AUT and SER evaluations, component ablations and analyses of reasoning and training dynamics.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds held-out results, additional baseline evaluations, automated reasoning assessments and a human evaluation.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-Omni-7B backbone, task/sample advantage modulation, geometric centering, inertial smoothing, rewards and optimization objective are unchanged. Appendix A's Algorithm 1 differs only in its equation cross-reference; moving the model setup into Section 3 does not change the method.

E1.justification: Table 2 expands held-out coverage from autism behavior recognition and speech emotion recognition to five contexts, adding in-the-wild depression recognition, social-media sentiment analysis and sarcasm incongruity recognition. The Human Behavior Atlas training coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Gemma 4-E4B, OmniSapiens SFT, OmniSapiens BAM and EMAGRPO to the retained comparators. Gemma 4-E4B also joins the held-out comparison in Table 2. These additions substantially broaden both model and optimization comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces systematic reasoning-evaluation protocols: answer agreement, paraphrase agreement, reasoning-token counts and masked pairwise human judgments. Appendix D specifies decoding configurations, a 512-token generation cap, fixed instruction paraphrases and three non-author annotators. The existing training budgets, checkpoint selection and predictive metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds stochastic-consistency and paraphrase-robustness tests, efficiency measurements and human assessments of specificity, coherence and concision. The original component ablations and HUM/SAR reasoning analyses are retained, although relocated. The detailed AUT overprediction, abstention and precision–recall analysis is removed.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports five independently sampled inference traces per input for consistency and average-token measurements (Table 3 and Appendix D). This concerns repeated inference, not additional training replications. Neither version reports training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results include OmniSapiens scores of 72.43, 58.47 and 69.27 on IDR, SMSA and SIR, plus automated and human reasoning outcomes in Tables 3–4. Retained per-task scores are unchanged. Expanded comparator sets change the model's average rank from 1.20 to 1.90 and HARPO's algorithm rank from 1.70 to 2.10; these are not same-setting performance declines. AUT diagnostic result entries are removed.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix D adds mathematical definitions of agreement across sampled predictions and agreement under paraphrasing, in Equations 13–14. The existing GRPO formulation and HARPO geometric-mean derivation remain unchanged, moving from Appendix D to Appendix E.

C1.justification: The central HARPO and unified-model contributions persist. v2 expands the reasoning claim to five named interpretability properties and recalibrates multitask superiority: the headline gain changes from +16.85% to +12.02%, while the discussion changes from best on nine tasks to top-two on eight tasks.

C2.justification: v2 interprets prediction agreement, brevity and human preferences through explicit XAI properties. It qualifies the proposed connection between balanced learning and transfer as requiring further investigation, and explains why SFT/BAM classifier heads preclude zero-shot evaluation. Conversely, it removes v1's substantive AUT qualification that improved precision comes with lower recall.

D1.justification: New Appendix D documents decoding parameters, tokenizer-based length measurement, paraphrase controls, annotator backgrounds, masking and annotation instructions. v2 also supplies a model/code repository link and states that these resources are released, replacing v1's post-review availability promise. Existing training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands its social-intelligence and interpretability positioning, adding foundations such as Baron-Cohen and Goleman and XAI evaluation literature including Langer, Nauta and Turbé. It also introduces EMAGRPO through Feng et al. as a multitask-balancing comparator. Several earlier motivation references disappear, although the core reinforcement-learning related-work discussion remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statement and conclusion are substantially rewritten around the model and its interpretability. Model setup moves from the experiments into Section 3; reasoning evaluation and algorithm analyses are reorganized; a new Appendix D shifts subsequent appendices. Affiliations, publication information and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds two reasoning-evaluation tables and a boxed annotation guide, expands the main comparison and held-out tables, and enlarges the appendix comparison table. All seven figures are retained, but the main figures are reordered and relocated, including v1 Figures 1–2 becoming v2 Figures 4–5.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical case by addressing limited held-out coverage and missing strong comparators, while adding documented automated and masked human reasoning evaluations. The broader comparison also appropriately reduces the headline multitask gain. These benefits outweigh the loss of the useful AUT recall qualification. Reporting weaknesses remain: human-study sample counts are unspecified, and some Table 4 win rates contradict Appendix D's formula—for example, 80.6% Tie+Win and 35.3% Tie imply about 70.0% wins excluding ties, rather than the reported 66.0%.
